questions: How many bars did you pattern and measure from the 2.0 nm heterostructure, and how many showed a field-free diode effect? You show two (Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 4).
Why were the others set aside, if any were?

Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: η against temperature up to the 350 mK Tc, η in small applied fields around zero, [100] preparation beyond ±1 T, and step delays or voltage thresholds other than 0.2 s and 50 µV?
What does the second-best dataset look like, for example a second cooldown of the [010] bar, and what sign did η take after each zero-field cooldown?
How did you set H = 0 after each preparation field? Was the residual field of the magnet measured, and do the [100] and [010] preparations use different coils or a rotated sample?

Does a polarity written by the preparation field survive warming the bar above the Al Tc at H = 0 and cooling again? Flux trapped in the Al would be erased by that step, while the Néel state (TN = 480 K) should be kept.

Did you measure a plain Al bar of the same width with the same protocol, and how does the SQUID bound of 3×10−3 µB/Mn (about 0.8 mT in µ0M by my estimate) compare with the applied field at which such a bar shows a diode effect?

The Néel-state readout in Fig. 4 comes from a different wafer with a 3 nm oxidized Al cap, measured at 5 K. Have you read out the Néel state on the superconducting heterostructure itself after the same protocol, and what couples the sign of the preparation field to L+ or L− in a magnet with zero net moment?
